Author: Krishan Pahal

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 83
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 27737 of 2019
Applicant :- Pradeep @ Lala
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P.And Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Som Veer,Anita Singh,Azhar Hussain,Prakash Chand,Prem Babu Verm
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Shri Ram (Rawat)
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. Heard Sri Som Veer, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri Yogesh Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the
State and perused the record.
2. None present on behalf of the informant even in revise call.
3. Applicant seeks bail in Case Crime No.168 of 2019, under Sections 376 I.P.C. and Section 5D/6
Pocso Act, Police Station Etmaddaula, District Agra, during the pendency of trial.
4.

sentences.text:
As per the prosecution story, the applicant who happens to be relative of informant, is said to
have sexually assaulted the infant daughter of informant aged about 4 months in her house on
3.3.2019 at about 1:30 P.M.

Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the applicant had given Rs. 50,000/- to the
informant and had demanded for its return, as such he has been falsely implicated in the case.
Learned counsel has stated that the informant suspected the applicant to have illicit relationship with his wife, as such also, he has been falsely implicated in the case.
Learned counsel has further stated that engagement ceremony of the applicant was solemnized on 2.3.2019 and his marriage was solemnized on 13.3.2019.
Thus, there is no possibility of the applicant committing the said offence on 03.03.2019.
He further stated that the FIR has been lodged after a delay of 11 days and there is no explanation of the said delay.
Learned counsel has further stated that although P.W.-1, who is the informant of the case, has supported the prosecution story, but he is not an eye-witness to the incident.
Learned counsel has further stated that P.W.-2, who is the mother of the victim, is the eye-witness to the incident, has also not supported the prosecution story during her cross-examination.
Learned counsel has further stated that as such there is no likelihood of conviction of the applicant in the matter.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 15.3.2019.

6. Per contra, learned A.G.A. has opposed the bail application and stated that it is itself evident from the FIR that a fact has been mentioned by the informant that the applicant is nephew, as such he was avoiding to lodge FIR against him, but as his daughter was continuously not getting well, he had to lodge the present FIR against the applicant, after a delay of 11 days.
He further stated that the injury report categorically corroborates the prosecution story and the injury has been found on the private part of the victim.
The victim is a child of four months and the circumstances have been narrated by P.W.-1 and P.W.-2 also.
He also stated that the statement of P.W.-1 recorded on 25.1.2021, the mother of the victim, was intact during her cross-examination.
The case was adjourned and on 8.10.2021 the said witness has not supported the prosecution story during the said cross-examination.

7. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the victim is a child of four months only and also the fact that prosecution witnesses have supported the version alleged in the FIR, I do not find it a fit case for bail.
8. The bail application is, accordingly, rejected.

9. However, it is directed that the aforesaid case pending before the trial court be decided expeditiously, preferably within a period of one year from the date of production of a certified copy of this order or as early as possible in view of the principle as has been laid down in the recent judgements of the Apex Court in the cases of Vinod Kumar Vs. State of Punjab; 2015 (3) SCC 220 and Hussain and Another vs. Union of India; (2017) 5 SCC 702, if there is no legal impediment.
